claims.text: Severe cryo-rolling followed by annealing can tailor a heterogeneous microstructure.
This processing route can overcome the strength-ductility trade-off in brittle intermetallic-containing high-entropy alloys.
The studied material is CoCrFeNi2.1Nb0.2, with an FCC matrix containing complex Laves-phase particles.
The ingots were homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h.
The material was multi-pass cold- or cryo-rolled to 90% thickness reduction and a final thickness of approximately 0.4 mm.
Cryo-rolling included immersion in liquid nitrogen for 0.5 h before and after every pass.
Rolling was followed by annealing at 800 °C for 1 h and water quenching.
The resulting heterogeneous microstructure contains coexisting deformed and recrystallized regions.
Cryo-rolling produces a greater density of precipitation nucleation sites, including dislocations, shear bands, and grain boundaries.
The greater density of nucleation sites accelerates nanosized ε-phase precipitation early during recrystallization.
The nanosized ε-phase precipitates pin high-angle boundaries through Zener pinning.
Boundary pinning inhibits recrystallization and creates a mixture of deformed and recrystallized regions.
Mechanical incompatibility between deformed and recrystallized domains generates strain gradients and geometrically necessary dislocations.
The geometrically necessary dislocations create long-range back stress.
Long-range back stress delays necking and enhances both strength and ductility.
The cryo-rolled and annealed alloy has a yield strength of 1219 ± 14 MPa and an ultimate tensile strength of 1272 ± 25 MPa.
The cryo-rolled and annealed alloy has approximately 22% elongation.
The cold-rolled and annealed baseline has a yield strength of 774 ± 13 MPa, an ultimate tensile strength of 1085 ± 18 MPa, and approximately 20% elongation.
The back stress generated by the heterogeneous microstructure was not quantified in the study.
The stability of the nanodomains during long-term storage and deformation is not fully understood.
